newsitem.title: CHINA: Russia deputy PM to visit China Three Gorges dam.
newsitem.headline: Russia deputy PM to visit China Three Gorges dam.

text.p: Russia's First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov has suddenly changed his itinerary in China to visit the Three Gorges dam at the invitation of Premier Li Peng, Russian officials said on Wednesday.

Nemtsov, who is also minister of fuel and energy, is in Beijing to work out details of several energy and trade agreements before the arrival in China on Thursday of Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin.
"Nemtsov will go to (the Three Gorges) tomorrow instead of accompanying the prime minister," a spokesman for the Russian embassy in Beijing said.
A Russian consortium is bidding for a contract to supply 14 generators with a total installed capacity of 9,800 megawatts for the Three Gorges hydroelectric power station on the Yangtze River.

The spokesman said it was unclear if Nemtsov's sudden change of plans was related to Russia's bid to participate in the huge hydropower and water conservancy project, which is scheduled for completion in 2009 at an estimated cost of 240 billion yuan ($28.9 billion).
"We do not know yet why he has been called down there," the spokesman said.

The China Yangtze Three Gorges Development Corp has said it was still reviewing tenders from several consortia to supply the generating units and had planned to select the winning bidder by late June or early July.

Other groups in the running include Siemens AG and GE Canada; Anglo-French group GEC Alsthom ; Swedish-Swiss ABB; a Japanese group; Impsa of Agentina, and Westinghouse of Canada, official media has said.
Diplomats said Chernomyrdin's visit is aimed at improving lagging economic ties with China after a series of high-level exchanges have bolstered political relations between Moscow and Beijing.
